title: LSTM-designed peptides show antibacterial activity and mixed efficacy in a mouse sepsis model
summary: A generative long short-term-memory recurrent neural network produced 198 candidate antimicrobial peptides; five were synthesized. PEP-38 and PEP-137 inhibited carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella isolates in vitro, and PEP-137 also inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa. In a small mouse K. pneumoniae sepsis experiment, PEP-137 yielded 50% survival, PEP-38 did not improve survival, and the in-vitro-inactive PEP-36 control unexpectedly yielded 66.7% survival.
ai_technology: Generative long short-term memory recurrent neural network trained on antimicrobial peptide sequences

evidence.tested: In a small mouse K. pneumoniae sepsis experiment, PEP-137 yielded 50% survival, PEP-38 did not improve survival, and the in-vitro-inactive PEP-36 control unexpectedly yielded 66.7% survival.
evidence.unknown: Only 5/198 AI-generated peptides were synthesized. The animal experiment used one administration, small groups (12 mice per group) and a simple model; PEP-36's unexpected survival effect despite no in-vitro antibacterial activity complicates interpretation. PEP-38 did not improve survival; no mechanism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics or safety was established. These are exploratory preclinical results, not a treatment claim.
evidence.ai_role: The LSTM RNN generated 198 peptide sequences, which were further filtered in silico; five selected candidates were synthesized and assayed. Two showed in-vitro activity against carbapenem-resistant isolates, and two were advanced into a mouse sepsis study.
